title: How Wide Can French Spreads Get?
gist: The French OAT-bund 10-year spread widened 40bp over the last three weeks of September 2026 to 127bp, a level last seen in June 2012 just before Draghi's 'whatever it takes'. Gavekal argues today differs from the euro crisis: France is now the epicentre with outright rising yields, rather than a bystander whose spread widened only because bund yields fell faster.

insights.claim: The spread between 10-year French OATs and 10-year German bunds widened 40bp over the last three weeks of September 2026, reaching 127bp on 30 September.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Rapid, sizeable repricing of French sovereign risk; momentum in spread widening is a live risk for euro rates books.
insights.quote: the sovereign yield spread between 10-year French OATs and 10-year German bunds widened 40bp, hitting 127bp on Wednesday
insights.locator: Over the last three weeks of September

insights.claim: A 127bp OAT-bund spread matches levels last seen in June 2012, weeks before Mario Draghi's 'whatever it takes' speech, prompting investors to draw euro-crisis parallels.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Spreads are at historic stress levels where the market previously needed central-bank backstop language to stabilise.
insights.quote: That is a gap last seen in June 2012, just weeks before Mario Draghi’s “whatever it takes” speech.
insights.locator: Over the last three weeks of September

insights.claim: Unlike the euro crisis, when France was a bystander and its spread widened only because German yields fell faster than falling French yields, French yields are now rising outright.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Today's widening reflects France-specific credit/fiscal concern, not flight-to-quality into bunds, so it implies genuine repricing of French risk rather than a relative-value artefact.
insights.quote: Through much of the euro crisis, French yields were actually falling; the widening of the French spread occurred because German yields fell faster. Today, French yields are rising outright

insights.claim: France has shifted from an 'unfortunate bystander' in the periphery-centred euro crisis to the frontier of eurozone spread widening today.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A core eurozone sovereign at the centre of stress is systemically different from a periphery crisis; policy responses and contagion channels may differ.
insights.quote: France is at the frontier of eurozone spread widening

insights.claim: During the euro crisis the stress centred on peripheral economies, with Greece's sovereign spread at one point exceeding 3,500bp, illustrating how far spreads can go when a true periphery crisis unfolds.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Historical upper bound context for how wide eurozone spreads can get; French 127bp remains far from crisis-periphery extremes.
insights.quote: That episode centered on the eurozone’s peripheral economies, notably Greece, whose spread at one point exceeded 3,500bp.
